description: Bean qou-wgnx. Off-axis structure of the connection invariant chi, plus a PRECISION WARNING for the sibling scripts. (1) At DPS=120/NG=500/NH=60 — the settings of c3_w2_c1_connection_invariant.py, ample on the real axis — an off-axis evaluation at z = 0.42i has entrywise P-ellipticity deviation ~1.1, i.e. NO signal, and reports log10|chi| = -45.8 where the converged value is -73.4468. Since P(pz) = P(z) is an algebraic identity, that deviation is a pure error meter and must be checked before believing any off-axis number. (2) REFLECTION LAW chi(conj z) = 1/conj(chi(z)), verified to 1e-167, because the real-coefficient operator makes conjugation swap the two 0-side solutions and hence P's rows. Consequently |chi| = 1 on the real axis is AUTOMATIC, not independent connection data — a correction to how the earlier result reads. (3) Off-axis, |chi| is independent of |z| to ~10 digits and log|chi| is exactly linear in arg z with slope -2 pi/(log p ln 10), i.e. chi behaves like z^(i 2 pi/log p) in a sector, then SATURATES with the bend near arg/pi = 0.447 = arg(-t2)/pi, a 0-side exponent direction. Sector-wise power behaviour switching across exponent rays is the signature of a theta quotient. NOT DETERMINED: chi's divisor, hence not its closed form. Stokes multipliers remain OPEN.

results.consequence: |chi| = 1 on the real axis is automatic
results.off_axis_behaviour: z^(i 2 pi / log p) in a sector, saturating near arg(-t2)

verdict: Off the real axis chi behaves like z^(i 2 pi/log p) in a sector — log|chi| linear in arg z with slope matching -2 pi/(log p ln 10) exactly, and |z|-independent — then saturates, the bend sitting at arg(-t2), a 0-side exponent direction. Sector-wise power behaviour switching across exponent rays is the signature of a theta quotient, so chi is presumably a ratio of theta_p's in the exponents and T. TWO CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER READINGS: |chi| = 1 on the real axis follows from the reflection law chi(conj z) = 1/conj(chi(z)) and is not independent data; and the sibling scripts' settings, though ample on the real axis, carry NO off-axis signal — always check entrywise P-ellipticity first, since P(pz) = P(z) is an algebraic identity and therefore a pure error meter. NOT DETERMINED: chi's divisor, hence not its closed form; an elliptic function is fixed by its divisor up to a constant and the sector data constrains but does not supply it. Stokes multipliers remain OPEN.
